title: Duplicate handler registration silently overwrites despite documented rejection
reasoning: The register docstring declares ValueError on an already registered message_type, but the implementation only logs a warning and overwrites the existing handler. That makes handler ownership order-dependent and can replace an existing route without a hard failure, which is especially risky for WebSocket message routing where duplicate message types should be caught during startup or test setup.
recommendation: Either enforce the documented contract by raising ValueError on duplicate registration, or intentionally change the API to make replacement explicit with a separate replace/override path and update docs/tests accordingly.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked registry tests are included, and this mismatch would only be caught by a test that registers the same message type twice and asserts the intended duplicate behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a registry unit test that registers a message type twice and asserts ValueError is raised, or, if replacement is intentional, asserts replacement only occurs through an explicit override API.
minimumFixScope: backend/src/api/infrastructure/registry.py plus a focused registry duplicate-registration test.
